messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Cross-Classified Models in Stan
parts:
I had been struggling last year using Stan with a particular type of model where firms are organized in a sector and industry hierarchy, but also by countries. So there's two hierarchies in it. At the time, I didn't know what it was called, but I just found out it is called a cross-classified model. I found a reference here:

Rasbash, J. and Goldstein, H. (1994) Efficient analysis of mixed hierarchical and cross classified random structures using a multilevel model. Journal of Educational and Behavioural Statistics, 19: 337-350.

Bristol University seems to have a decent amount of materials on this. The documentation for MLwiN discusses this approach. Their examples correspond well to the school example from Stan, except that it adds in a neighborhood.

I'm curious if anyone has tried anything like this in Stan.

messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cross-Classified Models in Stan
parts:
I've read Gelman and Hill, actually a few times at this point. It focuses on the hierarchical case. Cross-classification might be thought of as multilevel, but it is not the same thing as hierarchical.

To flesh out what I was saying above a bit more, consider the basic school example that is used in the RStan Quick Start guide (among other places). Imagine that there is also a neighborhood grouping, such that a student from school A could be a member of neighborhood A, but another student from school A could be a member of neighborhood B. A student from school B similarly could be from neighborhood A or B. So the grouping is not nested/hierarchical. From a social science perspective, this might be relevant in some cases.

The approach corresponds to my firm/sector/country example because you might have firms that have similar characteristics because they are in the same sector or because they are int he same country. My alternative was to just make a hierarchical decision to go country->country_sector->country_industry. However, you're implicitly assuming that sector A in country A is uncorrelated with sector A in country B, which is not the case.

When I was previously trying to estimate the cross-classification structure in Stan (i.e. not the hierarchical one), my problem was that it was overidentified. I had a mean for country and a mean for sector in the mean equation and they would blow up.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Cross-Classified Models in Stan
parts:
What Michael said. You just have to make sure not
to create an identifiability problem. For instance, if
you have a simple multilevel model with voters grouped by
state of residence and by sex, then you can have a
varying-intercept model for each, but they should both get
0 means because you'll have a general intercept and all you model
by group is difference from the "mean" behavior of the group.

So you'd have alpha1 varying by state, alpha2 varying by sex,
and a single parameter alpha for an intercept:

y[n] ~ inv_logit(alpha1[state[n]] + alpha2[sex[n]] + alpha);
alpha1 ~ normal(0,sigma_alpha1);
alpha2 ~ normal(0,sigma_alpha2);
sigma_alpha1 ~ ...
sigma_alpha2 ~ ...
alpha ~ ...

If you try to assign a hierarchical mean for alpha1 and alpha2, the
model's not identified. This isn't Stan, it's just a fact about
the likelihood.

- Bob
